items.explanation: 年 means year and is read ネン in most words, as in 来年 (らいねん, next year) and in dates like 2026年. This year, 今年, has the special reading ことし.
items.mnemonic: A farmer carrying a sheaf of rice: one harvest every year.

items.explanation: 時 means time and o'clock. It is read ジ: 三時 (さんじ) is three o'clock. Watch out for 四時 (よじ) and 九時 (くじ). Time in general is じかん.
items.mnemonic: The sun (日) next to a temple (寺) bell that rings the hours.

items.explanation: 分 means minute and to divide. Minutes are フン, which becomes ぷん after some numbers: 一分 (いっぷん), 三分 (さんぷん), 十分 (じゅっぷん). The verb わかる (to understand) is written 分かる.
items.mnemonic: A knife (刀) under 八, whose two strokes fall apart: something divided.

items.explanation: 半 means half and is read ハン. Put it after a time to say half past: 三時半 (さんじはん) is 3:30.
items.mnemonic: A vertical line cutting a shape exactly in half.

items.explanation: 今 means now and is read いま alone. The on reading コン appears in 今月 (こんげつ, this month). Today, 今日, has the special reading きょう.
items.mnemonic: A roof over a single moment: right now.
